title: Even Three-Digit Numbers From Tiles
statement:
You have a pile of digit tiles, given as an array tiles where each entry is a digit from 0 to 9. The same digit may appear on several tiles.

Pick three different tiles and lay them in a row to form a number. Keep it only if it is a real three-digit number (the first tile is not 0) and it is even.

Return every number you can build this way, each one once, in increasing order.

examples.why: It must end in 0 or 4 and cannot start with 0. 034 and 043 are not three-digit numbers, and 403 is odd.
Two 6 tiles let 6 appear twice. 166 and 616 are even, 661 is not.
No even digit at all, so nothing can end the number.

hints: There are only 450 even three-digit numbers. Could you test each one instead of combining tiles?
Count how many tiles show each digit. A number is buildable if, for every digit, it uses no more copies than you have.
Loop from 100 to 998 in steps of 2, count the digits of the candidate, and compare with the tile counts.

explain.intuition:
Combining tiles directly means picking ordered triples from up to 100 tiles, about a million choices, plus deduplicating. Flip it around: the answer space is tiny. There are only 450 even numbers from 100 to 998.

Count the tiles per digit once. For each candidate, count its own digits and check none needs more copies than the pile has. Walking candidates in increasing order also hands you the sorted, duplicate-free output for free.
steps: Build have[d], the number of tiles showing digit d.
For x from 100 to 998 in steps of 2, split it into its three digits.
Count the digits of x and check need[d] ≤ have[d] for each.
If it fits, push x. Return the list.
pitfalls: Checking only that each digit is present. 222 needs three 2 tiles, not one.
Building from index triples and forgetting to dedupe: [6, 6, 1] produces 616 twice from the two 6 tiles.
Allowing a leading 0, which yields two-digit numbers like 034.

solutions.title: All ordered triples of tiles
solutions.idea: Try every choice of three different tile positions, keep valid numbers in a set, then sort.

solutions.title: Test every even candidate against digit counts
solutions.idea: Only 450 candidates exist. Keep the ones whose digit counts fit inside the tile counts.

followups: Return numbers of any length L instead of 3. When does enumerating candidates stop being cheaper than building from tiles?
Only count the results without listing them. Can you do it with arithmetic on the digit counts?
